data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --time=12:00:00
#   --gres=gpu:k20:0
#   --cpus-per-task=1
#   --mem=4G
#   -o ./results/slurm-%A_%a.out

#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=12h

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=4G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: -o with %A/%a tokens
# Slurm tokens %A (job id) and %a (array index) are not portable in Flux output directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

# Note on Slurm GPU request: --gres=gpu:k20:0
# This requests ZERO GPUs. No Flux GPU request is needed.
# Performance implication: none.

module load imkl/2018.3.222
module load openmpi/3.1.2
module load cuda/10.0.130
module load python/3.7

source /project/cq-training-1/project1/teams/team06/ift6759-env/bin/activate

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:/cvmfs/soft.computecanada.ca/easybuild/software/2017/avx2/Compiler/intel2016.4/cuda/10.0.130/extras/CUPTI/lib64

python evaluator.py predictions.txt data/admin_cfg.json -u data/user_cfg.json

reasons: The original Slurm job requested 4G of memory (`--mem=4G`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.
